chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hafs ibn Suqah from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is that thing in which there is no vow?' He said: 'Whatever you have benefit in for religion or worldliness, there is no sin upon you if you do not fulfill it.'

key_terms.حِنْث: Sin or fault incurred by breaking a vow
key_terms.نَذْر: Vow, a voluntary commitment to do something for God's sake

ai.seo_question: When is a vow (nadhr) considered binding in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the condition of benefit (manfa'a) for the binding nature of vows, linking religious and worldly utility to the absence of sin (hinth) upon non-fulfillment. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that vows are not absolute obligations but are contingent upon their substantive value, distinguishing them from mandatory duties. The emphasis on 'benefit' underscores the pragmatic approach of the Ahl al-Bayt in regulating personal commitments to prevent undue hardship.
